You are a careful research assistant helping write the network-science background subsection of a PhD dissertation introduction (network science, Northeastern). The dissertation asks why an individual's chance of being selected (drafted, promoted, tenured, admitted) should be studied as a function of the environment (peers + organization) and not only of individual performance. Three channels: development (what a person becomes), evaluation (how a given performance is measured/perceived), selection (who wins a scarce slot). Sources: peers vs organization. A key interest: how network science represents organizations (affiliation/bipartite networks of persons and groups), how local position shapes outcomes, and how status/prestige hierarchies form.

YOUR JOB: read a set of papers from PDFs and write ONE markdown note file with accurate, verbatim, page-cited extracts. Do NOT write prose for the dissertation. Never invent numbers.

import re,subprocess
t=open('FOUNDY_Intro.bib',encoding='utf-8').read()
ents=re.split(r'\n(?=@)',t)
want=['granovetter_strength_1973','centola_complex_2007','burt_structural_2004','burt_structural_1992','barabasi_emergence_1999','clauset_systematic_2015','nikolaev_modeling_2023','geard_competition_2010','uzzi_collaboration_2005','newman_assortative_2002','feld_why_1991','guimera_team_2005','colizza_detecting_2006','mason_collaborative_2012','lazer_network_2007','gould_origins_2002','breiger_duality_1974','lazer_computational_2020','lazer_computational_2009']

    f=re.search(r'file\s*=\s*\{(.+?)\}',e,re.S).group(1)

    print(k.group(1), pages.group(1) if pages else '?', len(open(out).read()))
